transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-07
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rafael Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Elysian Head of Search), Tom Adler (Elysian Lead ML Eng), Zoe Park (Elysian PM)

Summary (auto): Quick hosted API demo of embeddings + reranker, followed by Q&A on performance and security. Action items captured.

00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
00:06 Priya Nair: Priya here, hi.
00:08 Tom Adler: Tom on the line.
00:11 Zoe Park: Zoe, hi all.
00:13 Maya Chen: Great, I'm Maya from Redwood, and Rafael is my SE, he'll drive the deep bits. Rafael, you want to intro?
00:18 Rafael Ortiz: Yeah hi, Rafael Ortiz, I'm the solutions engineer, I work on retrieval/rerank patterns and infra. We'll show a hosted flow — embeddings + reranker — and then the console traces and Optimize suggestions.
00:30 Priya Nair: High level goal: improve product search relevancy — particularly long-tail queries and new SKUs. We're seeing poor ordering for intent queries and we want better MRR and fewer zero-clicks.
00:40 Maya Chen: Perfect. Quick qualification: current infra?
00:43 Tom Adler: We're running an ES cluster for indexing, some Redis for sessions. We tested Pinecone for vectors but latency was variable and cost spiked. We have a batch job to index products nightly.
00:56 Rafael Ortiz: Good context. We'll demo two-stage: 1) embeddings search via hosted API for vector retrieve, 2) call to our reranker endpoint to rescore top-k. We'll show trade-offs: reranker length/size impacts latency.
01:12 Rafael Ortiz: I'll share my screen now — can you see the console? (screen share)
01:18 Zoe Park: Yep, seeing it.
01:20 Rafael Ortiz: Right, on the left is the hosted embeddings API playground. We're using a 'smallish' embedding model for this demo — that gives you good economy. For high precision you can pick a larger encoding.
01:36 Tom Adler: Do you expose model sizes and tokenization? We need to know dimension sizes for our vector DB.
01:41 Rafael Ortiz: Yes, the API returns dims in the model catalog. For the model I'm using today it's 1536 dims, so that matches many vector DBs. Sometimes the catalog label gets mis-typed in the export (we saw one as 1,536 in a prior CSV) — minor thing.
01:57 Priya Nair: Walk us through the end-to-end latency contribution from each stage?
02:02 Rafael Ortiz: Sure — embedding inference is usually ~20-40ms on hosted depending on model. Vector retrieval latency is your DB's concern — but we usually target top-100 retrieval within 20-60ms. Reranker call latency depends on model size and input length; for our production reranker a common SLO is 80-150ms for k=10 reranks using a 6B-class model on the hosted tier. Keep in mind continuous batching and our smart routing can reduce per-request cost.
02:30 Zoe Park: Smart routing as in fallback to smaller model when under load?
02:33 Rafael Ortiz: Exactly. Policy-based: cost-first or latency-first. You can pin a model version for consistency or allow fallbacks.
02:40 Priya Nair: Can we see the reranker request/response?
02:43 Rafael Ortiz: Sure — switching to the reranker endpoint tab. Example payload: query + candidate snippets + doc metadata. The response is a score + optional structured explanation tokens if you enable structured output.
02:58 Rafael Ortiz: Note: sometimes the transcript generator shows 'kay v cache' instead of 'KV cache' in logs — don't be surprised.
03:05 Tom Adler: ha, yep. On the candidate side, do you accept BM25+vector hybrid?
03:09 Rafael Ortiz: You can combine signals. Many customers run a hybrid: BM25 for recall, vector for semantic match; then reranker uses both the document text and BM25 score as features. We also have a built-in reranker feature store you can forward features to.
03:25 Priya Nair: What metrics should we track to measure improvement?
03:28 Rafael Ortiz: NDCG@10, MRR@5, recall@100 are standard. For ecomm we also monitor purchase-through-query and time-to-click; Redwood Console can surface per-route MRR and regression alerts tied to prompt sets or evals.
03:42 Zoe Park: show the Optimize tab?
03:44 Rafael Ortiz: Yep, coming up — Optimize suggests batching config, quantization profile recommendations, and prefix/KV cache settings based on observed sequence length distribution. Here is a recommendation we ran against a synthetic workload: batch size 8 for lower latency 90th pct, enable 4-bit quantization on the reranker for 2–3x token cost reduction with marginal score delta.
04:09 Priya Nair: Any quality drop with 4-bit?
04:12 Rafael Ortiz: Slight, you should run an eval on your ground-truth. For many rerankers 4-bit is fine; for top-of-funnel generation we usually avoid aggressive quant. The Console includes regression alerts if NDCG dips beyond threshold.
04:28 Tom Adler: Security: we need SOC2 docs, SSO, and KMS integration for keys. How do you handle customer data in hosted?
04:36 Maya Chen: Good question — hosted includes tenant isolation, optional VPC peering for private networking, and we support KMS/HSM for model keys and payload encryption at rest. We can share our SOC2 Type II report, and SAML SSO is supported; audit logs are available via the console. Rafael, anything more?
04:50 Rafael Ortiz: For extra-sensitive workloads we recommend Redwood Private. Hosted still supports strict retention policies and encryption. We'll share the security packet, and we can set up a call with security if needed.
05:02 Priya Nair: That helps. What about data residency? We need EU region hosting for part of our catalog.
05:08 Maya Chen: We have regional endpoints — you can pin routing to eu-west for specific customers or routes.
05:13 Zoe Park: show a live rerank example end-to-end?
05:16 Rafael Ortiz: Yep. I'll call embeddings endpoint with a long-tail query "women's waterproof running shoes size 9 wide".
05:23 Rafael Ortiz: // request sent // 00:05 response for embedding vector...
05:30 Rafael Ortiz: Pass top-200 to your vector DB (here simulated), then fetch top-10 candidates and call reranker. Reranker call payload — notice we include product metadata fields (brand, price, availability) as additional context.
05:48 Rafael Ortiz: Here is the reranker response — scores and the top re-ordered list. The console trace shows a 132ms reranker latency, embedding 28ms. 160ms end-to-end for k=10.
06:03 Tom Adler: 132ms seems a bit high for our SLA (aiming <120ms for UX). Any levers?
06:08 Rafael Ortiz: You can: reduce model size for reranker (e.g., Distil or 3B variant), shrink input length by truncating less-relevant doc fields, or enable batching at the edge which amortizes some cost. Also consider prefix/KV caching if queries include common prefixes.
06:22 Priya Nair: Do you do prefix caching automatically?
06:24 Rafael Ortiz: We have automatic prefix caching for repeated session prefixes and optional KV cache for chat-like flows; Optimize will recommend enabling it when it detects repetition patterns. For search queries it's more about deduplicating similar candidate contexts.
06:36 Zoe Park: What about cost modeling?
06:38 Maya Chen: The Console gives per-token cost breakdown by route and model. Also our billing export includes per-request cost attribution. For the pilot we can provide evaluation credits so you can run a benchmark without immediate spend.
06:51 Tom Adler: On retraining reranker: do you host fine-tuned weights or do we upload and serve?
06:55 Rafael Ortiz: Two patterns: 1) you provide a fine-tuned reranker and we host it (private or hosted depending on security), or 2) you host weights in your VPC and we provide serving glue. For hosted pilots many customers let Redwood host the reranker under an NDA and SOC2 boundary.
07:12 Priya Nair: Whoosh — earlier you mentioned fallback models. If we pin to a 6B reranker and that node goes offline, what's the graceful degradation?
07:20 Rafael Ortiz: The routing layer can fallback to a 3B variant in the same family and maintain output format; you can set a degradation budget so we only fallback when latency would otherwise breach SLO. We also support region failover.
07:33 Zoe Park: Any caveats about determinism between model versions?
07:36 Rafael Ortiz: Slight variability; that's why rollouts and A/Bs are important — Redwood supports canary rollouts and auto rollback on regression signals.
07:46 Priya Nair: Are there any customers in retail space you can reference?
07:49 Maya Chen: We can share case studies — several retail customers improved MRR by mid-single digits after rerankers and Optimize tuning. We'll include anonymized benchmarks.
07:58 Tom Adler: demo more of the Console traces — the token breakdown and per-route latency?
08:02 Rafael Ortiz: Scrolling. Here is token-level: embedding token counts are low, reranker is dominated by doc length. You can set per-route max_input_tokens in the API to limit cost.
08:19 Priya Nair: Show the eval UI?
08:21 Rafael Ortiz: Yep — this is Redwood Evals. You can upload labeled queries and candidates; it will run batch scoring and surface NDCG/MRR, and then tie alerts. We also keep historical baselines so you can see regressions over time.
08:38 Zoe Park: If we wanted to test the reranker only, can we pass precomputed embeddings?
08:41 Rafael Ortiz: Yes, reranker can accept precomputed vector features or raw text candidates. Many teams precompute embeddings offline and pass cached results to save embedding inference cost.
08:50 Tom Adler: For our pilot we'll likely do precompute + rerank on the hosted tier. What about payload size limits? We're shipping product descriptions that include HTML.
08:59 Rafael Ortiz: We suggest stripping HTML and sending cleaned text to the reranker; there is a payload limit (document length caps) — the console warns on truncation. For large docs we recommend indexing only description + top bullet points.
09:15 Priya Nair: On evaluation, how can we ensure annotation quality matters? We have sparse labels and ephemeral user signals.
09:21 Rafael Ortiz: You can weight queries or bootstrap via interleaving online A/B tests; Redwood supports evaluation weights per-query and combining offline and online metrics.
09:34 Zoe Park: any gotchas with vector DB connectors?
09:36 Rafael Ortiz: Connectors are straightforward; however, keep an eye on vector distance metric alignment (cosine vs euclidean) and normalization. We'll share a vector DB integration primer.
09:48 Priya Nair: Let's talk about latency tail — 95/99 percentiles — how do you help with that?
09:53 Rafael Ortiz: Autoscaling plus continuous batching helps; also reranker warm pools and pre-warming nodes for peak windows. For strict tails we recommend Dedicated or Private where we can reserve capacity.
10:06 Tom Adler: Dedicated capacity pricing — is that a separate contract?
10:09 Maya Chen: Yes, Dedicated is a reserved capacity product with commit terms. For pilot hosted is easiest; if you need guaranteed p99 you can opt into Dedicated. We'll include pricing options.
10:19 Priya Nair: How long to ramp from pilot to production? We're concerned about engineering lift.
10:23 Maya Chen: Many teams ship in 4–8 weeks from pilot start depending on dataset and integrations. Redwood SDKs and connector templates reduce friction. Rafael: we typically run a sprint — smoke tests, evaluation, and then a production rollout with canary.
10:36 Rafael Ortiz: For the pilot we can provide a sample repo: a retrieval + rerank pipeline with S3 ingestion, a vector db connector, and dashboard dashboards.
10:45 Zoe Park: Let's get more concrete — do you have a sample notebook you can share?
10:48 Rafael Ortiz: Yes, will share the notebook containing calls to embeddings endpoint, candidate construction, reranker call, and evaluation. It includes code to replay a batch job for 20k items.
10:58 Priya Nair: On the console, can we export traces to our APM?
11:01 Rafael Ortiz: Yes — traces can be exported to Datadog or Splunk; we also provide raw logs via retention export.
11:09 Tom Adler: Any limitation on request rate for hosted?
11:13 Maya Chen: Hosted has rate limits by default but you can request higher throughput; for high sustained QPS we recommend Dedicated.
11:21 Priya Nair: How do we instrument end-to-end user latency (client to final rerank) in Redwood?
11:26 Rafael Ortiz: We recommend adding a small client header and Redwood injects a trace id. Console maps per-route latency and spans so you can see embedding vs network vs rerank.
11:37 Zoe Park: Are there costs for trace retention and long-term observability?
11:40 Maya Chen: Yes, observability retention is an add-on; by default we retain 30 days and you can increase. We'll include details in the pricing doc.
11:51 Priya Nair: Let's talk about A/B testing with rerankers — do you handle traffic split?
11:55 Rafael Ortiz: Yes, canary and A/B split by percentage, user segment, or query type. We also do automatic regression detection and can auto rollback.
12:06 Tom Adler: Suppose we run reranker hosted but keep embeddings precomputed in our infra. Is that supported?
12:09 Rafael Ortiz: Yes, hybrid ops are common. You can push candidate payloads and skip embedding call. We also accept feature fields if you want to include offline signals.
12:18 Priya Nair: Any recommendations for cold-start SKUs?
12:21 Rafael Ortiz: Incorporate metadata signals (category, brand, price), use augmentation (title synonyms) and consider mixing generation for suggested keywords. The reranker can learn to prefer freshness signals if you include them as features.
12:34 Zoe Park: sample SLA numbers for hosted?
12:36 Maya Chen: Hosted SLAs are lower than Dedicated; we guarantee multi-regional availability and provide response time targets for paid tiers. We'll include exact numbers in the SLA packet.
12:47 Priya Nair: Security follow-up: can we get an architecture diagram for hosted network flow?
12:51 Maya Chen: We'll attach an architecture diagram and networking notes in the security pack.
12:58 Tom Adler: Are there known issues with common HTML sanitizers? We use some custom markups.
13:02 Rafael Ortiz: Our ingestion examples show standard sanitizer libs; for edge cases we recommend pre-cleaning. We'll include sample cleaning code.
13:10 Zoe Park: Can we do a short live benchmark run now? Maybe 1k queries?
13:14 Priya Nair: We have only 30 mins today, but a quick smoke would be nice.
13:18 Rafael Ortiz: We can run a small synthetic evaluation against a subset. I'll switch to the eval runner and upload a 200-query set.
13:26 Rafael Ortiz: Running... this will take ~2 minutes. Console shows running eval job — progress 30%... 60%...
13:45 Rafael Ortiz: Results: NDCG@10 improved from 0.42 baseline to 0.51 with reranker + hybrid retrieval. MRR@5 up from 0.34 to 0.44. Those numbers are synthetic but directionally promising.
14:02 Priya Nair: That's encouraging. Can you export the per-query diffs?
14:05 Rafael Ortiz: Yes, you can download CSV with per-query before/after ranks and model explanations.
14:12 Tom Adler: For the pilot we'll want to run your benchmark scripts against our labeled set; can we get the script?
14:16 Rafael Ortiz: Absolutely — will include it in the notebook.
14:22 Zoe Park: Any limitations on the reranker input format for multilingual titles? We have some EU locales.
14:26 Rafael Ortiz: Reranker supports unicode and multilingual encodings; we recommend running locale-specific embedding models for best results.
14:33 Priya Nair: Ok we're about halfway through — let's fast-forward Q&A items.
14:38 Tom Adler: Deployment question: for Dedicated, do you ship a config for autoscaling?
14:41 Maya Chen: Yes, Dedicated gives you more control: reserved GPU pools and autoscale policies tailored to workload. We usually do a sizing workshop.
14:50 Zoe Park: Pricing ask: can you provide an estimate for 2M queries/month with 10k product corpus?
14:55 Maya Chen: We'll model it with assumptions (embedding dims, reranker model, average tokens). I'll send an estimate in the pricing doc.
15:04 Priya Nair: Anything else on security?
15:07 Maya Chen: We'll attach SOC2, pen test summary, and KMS integration docs.
15:12 Tom Adler: Great. Next steps?
15:15 Maya Chen: Recap and next actions: Maya will send pricing + credits, Rafael will share notebook and eval scripts, Tom will send sample dataset and labels, and we'll schedule pilot kick-off.
15:28 Priya Nair: Sounds good. Thanks Rafael and Maya.
15:31 Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with links to the notebook, security pack, and next calendar invite.
15:38 Zoe Park: Thanks. Bye.
